Textbook: "The Cosmic Perspective" Bennett, Donahue, Schneider, Voit, Seventh Edition, Pearson New International Edition
📚 From Chapter 1 to 6, it mainly talks about astronomy, which focuses on how we look at the universe from the Earth to explain different scientific phenomenon, like solar eclispe, phases of Moon and how do we know the orbit of Earth around the Sun is elliptical.
📚 From Chapter 14 to 23, it mainly talks about space science covering a wide range of topics, such as different types of star Birth and death, different types of galaxies, black holes, Big Bang and dark matter.
✅ If you are interested in learning astronomy and space science, this course is suitable for you.
✅ You don't need to buy a textbook. I even did not use the textbook throughout the whole semester.
⚠️ However, if you don’t like learning physics concepts, formulas and doing calculations, please avoid this course as the exam contains a lot of conceptual and calculations questions.
Ch.1-2:
It starts by introducing a lot of basic astronomical concepts like different types of stars, look back time, astronomical unit (AU), which are fundamental of astronomy. They are quite boring if you don’t like to learn about physics concepts.
Then you have to imagine the sky as a big sphere called celestial sphere. The sphere is used to explain different astronomical concepts and phenomenon like zenith, zodiac, constellations, altitude and latitude and causes of seasons. If you are good at constructing 3D images in your head, these topics would be quite easy for you. Otherwise, you would be quite frustrating. The only solution for those who are not good at imagining is to memorize different facts and results, which is a pain in the butt.
After that, solar eclipse and lunar eclipse would be taught, including different phases and reasons. Again, if you are good at picturing the relative positions of Earth, Moon and Sun, you would be fine. Otherwise, you need to spend more efforts in understanding the concepts.
Ch.3:
It will introduce different astronomical models and concepts built in the history, from ancient Greek, Ptolemaic model, Copernican model, discoveries by Galileo to Kelper’s laws. While most of them are conceptual, you also need to perform calculations regarding to the Kelper’s laws. Therefore, you should pay efforts to familiarize with those concepts and calculations. Most of the topics in this chapter are covered in DSE Physics E1, so you would have great advantage if you have studied them before.
Ch.4:
This chapter is the MOST PHYSICS chapter as it introduces a lot of physics concepts, mostly with formulas. This includes Newton’s three laws of motion, circular motion, conservation of momentum, conservation of energy, gravitational potential energy, escape speed and tidal locking. 90% of this chapter is covered in DSE Physics ‘Force and Motion’ and E1, so if you have studied them before, you can easily handle them. Otherwise, it is quite difficult to handle all of them.
Ch.5:
In the first part, you will be introduced to the properties of light and thermal radiation, including v=fλ, absorption, emission and continuous line spectrum and fingerprints, stefan-boltzmann law, properties of blackboard radiation. Most of the content is covered in DSE Physics E1 and CHEM 1012 Ch.2. If you have studied them before, it is much easier to understand them, although these concepts are not too difficult for new learners.
In the second part, it talks about Doppler effects, which is again covered in DSE Physics E1 or PHYS 1111/1112. After that, it talks about angular resolving power, diffraction limit and different types of teloscopes with pros and cons. These contents are in fact quite boring, but they are not too deep in depth, so it would not be difficult to understand them.
Ch.14:
It talks about our Sun, including the structure of the Sun, nuclear fusion in the Sun and solar activities. These concepts are quite easy to understand, so you would have a honeymoon time in this chapter.
Ch.15:
It first talks about using Hipparchus Magnitude Scale, apparent and absolute magnitude to measure the brightness of a star, so you should expect there would be a bunch of equations you need to use. Most of them have been covered in DSE Physics E1, except m & M equation.
Then, it talks about H-R diagram, including lifetime of main sequence stars, main sequence line, equal radius line and turn-off line. Also, it introduces mass-luminosity relationship, luminosity class, different types of star clusters and binary systems. While some concepts have been taught in E1, you should spend some time to understand these concepts before the final exam.
Ch.16-17:
It first briefly introduces different types of nebula, and focus on the process of formation of a star, which involves many steps, so you should spend some time to familiarize them.
Then, it talks about the life of a low-mass, medium-mass star and high-mass star respectively. Each process involves many steps and astronomical concepts, but no calculations are required, so it is not too difficult to understand them.
Ch.18:
It mainly talks about white dwarf, supernova, black hole and neutron star. Although there are some calculations regarding to Schwarzschild radius and tidal forces of black holes, this chapter is not difficult to handle.
Ch.19:
It mainly talks about the Milky Way Galaxy, including its history, structure and characteristics. This part is quite interesting as we can learn our own galaxy. There is one calculation regarding to orbital-velocity law, which is quite easy.
Ch.20-21:
It mainly talks about different types of galaxies and how to use cosmic distance ladder to observe galaxies and stars in different distances. Also, it talks about cosmological redshift and galactical collisions between different galaxies, which relates to the future of the Milky Way Galaxy, making this part quite inspiring.
Ch.22-23:
It is the MOST ABSTRACT chapter among all chapters as this chapter mainly talks about dark matter and the future of the universe, which are something that scientists still cannot fully understand. Therefore, although this part contains many difficult concepts regarding to the dark matter, you don’t need to fully understand them to answer the questions in the exam.

This course focuses on Quantum Information Processing, which has the following topics:

教學涵蓋lecture同tutorial
Lecture方面（1小時20分鐘）：
professor主要是教公式的推導過程以及公式背後的物理意義，但考試不會叫你做公式推導。
本人DSE英文拿3，physics拿4，m2拿5。但是我覺得lecture堂公式推導的過程十分冗長和沉悶（可能因為我英文不好，上這堂課腦中要同時處理英文、物理和微積分，再加上飯後課，經常大腦過載陷入昏厥），學生必須時刻聽得懂每一步的數學推導在幹什麼，走一下神就會完全迷失，隨後完全不知道這一堂課在幹什麼。有感覺到Professor有嘗試讓這堂課變的有趣，課上會做些物理小實驗和舉一些生活化的例子。
還有lecture堂所教的calculus部分剛需m2，MATH1013到中期才學differentiation、最後幾堂課才會教integration、不會教任何vector基礎。所以上這門課之前你需要掌握的calculus的知識是：
- Differentiation（學到chain rule鏈式法則差不多了）
- Integration（學到代換積分法substitution差不多了）
- 3D vector基礎（dot / cross product只會在lecture課的公式推導和物理概念解釋,考試需要的vector知識就只是你要會分三個方向分別去d或者in）
這門課的內容會默認你已經熟悉這些calculus的知識，所以讀過m2的學生會有些許優勢
tutorial（50分鐘）
流程是先給你review一下這個星期或者上個星期的lecture學了些什麼，然後讓你做一張工作紙，做完對答案，最後會解答一題功課裡的題目。
我那個老師是個內地人，說英文很結巴，3句一小‘額...’，5句一大‘額......’，純靠語速來遮掩自己英文說不流暢的情況，這樣導致我在整堂課上都是一直再聽他額...額...額...，根本不知道再說什麼。所以lecture課的真正的流程是打開手機玩遊戲，等到老師解答工作紙答案的時候再抄，最後把工作紙交上去就結束了。

本人DSE英文拿3，physics拿4，m2拿5。
我感覺我拿B已經燃盡了，不建議在其他科都很大workload的情況下報這個。
每個禮拜都有一份homework，做一份會要你2~3個小時（如果你的DSE physics跟我一樣的話），一共14份（HW0,HW7,HW13不計分），但是我建議全部做，因為我認為這個課做功課的時候你會遇到這個流程：做homework → 不會做 → 問AI → 新知識get（其實課上早說過了），然后你會發現你做功課學到的東西比在lecture學到的多。
學習技巧：
1.建議考試前一周/兩周重做一次所有homework，一是可以練習解題的思路，二是因為考試有部分題目會照抄功課題目。
2.建議想我一樣英文不好的學生可以在考試溫習之前或者上lecture課之前把lecture note丟進AI，並附上以下語句：
 “我是一名智力低下的大学生，我想学习一下这篇筆記教了什麼，请用傻子都能听得懂的语言给我描述一下这篇笔记是在讲什么的，并在某些专有名词上给出英文翻译（考试用英文考的），还有特别是其中的公式推导以及原理，最后给出所有做相关题目时的常用公式，不要篡改原文内容，不要偏离文章核心。”
來預習、複習lecture note教了什麼。如果懶得放也沒關係，我會把我生成的放在附件裡。
